pattern.short_summary: Rather than reusing a standard chart type, the system introduces a new graphical mark whose geometry is designed around the specific property being communicated.
pattern.definition: Rather than reusing a standard chart type, the system introduces a new graphical mark whose geometry is designed around the specific property being communicated. The mark's parts each carry a distinct component of that property, and the mapping is defined by the paper. The encoding is a contributed object in its own right, described part by part.
pattern.structural_signature: A composite graphical mark is defined by an explicit mapping from named components of the data property to named geometric channels of the mark (sector angle, chord endpoint, block extent, static shape standing for a time-varying quantity). The definition is enumerable — the paper can label the parts — and the mark is instantiated once per unit of data. Transplantable in the sense that any property with named components can be given such a mark; but note that what is shared across instances is the *act of designing* a mark, and the marks themselves have nothing structural in common beyond compositeness.
